Research_Question: Do refactoring-containing commits exhibit different test-level missed-failure behavior in the specified history-based ML-PTS formulation than comparable non-refactoring commits?
Hypothesis: Refactoring-containing commits are associated with increased PTS test-level missed-failure rates compared to non-refactoring commits.
Falsification_Condition: The test-level miss behavior for refactoring-containing commits is statistically indistinguishable from or lower than non-refactoring commits.

Research_Question: Which classes of structural refactoring (identity-changing vs. identity-preserving) are associated with differences in missed-failure behavior and/or PTS feature distribution?
Hypothesis: Identity-changing refactorings exhibit significantly higher missed-failure rates and feature distribution shift than identity-preserving refactorings.
Falsification_Condition: Identity-preserving refactorings exhibit the same or higher feature distribution shift and miss behavior as identity-changing refactorings.

Research_Question: To what extent does preserving historical code identity through structural mapping attenuate any observed performance difference?
Hypothesis: Preserving structural identity reduces missed-failure behavior if the failure is caused by representation shift.
Falsification_Condition: Identity-aware PTS interventions (e.g., mapping renamed files) result in the same or higher test-level miss behavior compared to the baseline model.

Research_Question: Do AST/dependency structural features improve robustness on refactoring commits?
Hypothesis: Injecting structural features improves test-level recall on refactoring-containing commits compared to the baseline model.
Falsification_Condition: Structural features provide no statistically significant improvement in test-level recall on refactoring-containing commits.
